name: Knock Poker
description: Knock Poker (also known as Rap Poker) is an American draw and discard game in which the aim is to collect the best five-card poker hand. Unlike traditional poker, there is no betting process of raising and folding. Instead, players draw cards from a stock pile or take the previous player's discard, with the ability to 'knock' to end the round when they believe they have the strongest hand.

history.origins: Knock Poker emerged in the United States in the early 20th century as a non-gambling alternative to traditional poker. It was documented in Albert Ostrow's 'The Complete Card Player' (1945) and later in Scarne's 'Encyclopedia of Games' (1973).
timeline: 1940s: First documented in American card game literature
1973: Featured in Scarne's Encyclopedia of Games
1981: Included in 'The New Complete Hoyle Revised'
1999: Published in Bicycle Official Rules of Card Games
history.cultural: Popular as a family-friendly alternative to betting poker, often played for chips or small stakes among casual players.
history.evolution: The game evolved from Whisky Poker, changing the card collection method from exchanging with a face-up hand to drawing from a stock pile or discard pile. Unlike poker variants, it was never intended for dealer's choice poker games.

setup.players: 3 to 5 players optimal. Can be played with 2 or more than 5 using the same rules.
setup.dealing: Cards are shuffled, cut by the player to dealer's right, and dealt one at a time until each player has five cards. The remainder forms a draw pile, with the top card turned face up to start the discard pile.
setup.equipment: Poker chips or coins for scoring and a central pot.

rules.objective: Collect the best five-card poker hand and be the first to knock when confident of having the strongest hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Ante**: Each player pays one chip to the central pot before the deal.
2. **Turn Structure**: Players take turns clockwise, starting with the player to dealer's left.
3. **Drawing**: On your turn, draw one card either from the top of the stock pile (face down) or take the top card of the face-up discard pile.
4. **Knocking (Optional)**: If you believe you have the best poker hand, you may knock by knocking on the table or saying 'I knock'. This signals that play will end after each other player has one more turn.
5. **Discarding**: After drawing (and optionally knocking), discard one card face up on the discard pile. You cannot discard the same card you just took from the discard pile in the same turn.
6. **Immediate Knock**: A player satisfied with their original dealt hand may knock on their first turn without drawing or discarding.
keyRules: Draw from stock or discard pile each turn
Best poker hand wins the pot

strategy.basic: Know your poker hand rankings thoroughly. Knock when you have at least a strong pair or better, especially if few cards have been drawn from the stock.
strategy.intermediate: Watch the discard pile carefully. If you see high cards being discarded, it suggests opponents are building specific hands. If you see low cards discarded, opponents may be aiming for straights or flushes.
strategy.advanced: Timing your knock is critical. Knock early with a decent hand if you think opponents haven't had time to improve. Wait longer if you have a very strong hand and want to lure opponents into staying in. Consider the pot size - a larger pot justifies knocking with a slightly weaker hand.
tips: Don't be afraid to fold after a knock if your hand is weak - losing 1 chip is better than losing 2 plus the chance at the pot.
If you draw from the discard pile, you're revealing information about what you're collecting. Use the stock pile for secrecy.
The player who knocked has an advantage in knowing exactly when play ends - use this if you're the knocker.

variations.name: Simple Settlement
variations.description: Knock ends play immediately with no additional turns. Best hand simply takes the pot with no other payments.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes settlement timing only; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Ante Per Draw
variations.description: Each player adds an extra chip to the pot each time they draw a card.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule described in text; engine cost would require buyCosts or constants if implemented.

variations.name: Minimum Knock Requirement
variations.description: Players can only knock with a minimum hand such as a pair of Jacks or a pair of Aces.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Minimum hand for knock is a rule variant; no existing engine path for this constraint.

variations.name: Bonus Wins
variations.description: Extra bonuses paid by all players: 2 chips for knocking on first turn without drawing, 4 chips for royal flush, 2 chips for straight flush, 1 chip for four of a kind.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Bonus payouts are scoring extras; would need scoring overrides if implemented.

variations.name: Dompe
variations.description: Mexican variant played with a Joker as wild card and possibility of winning with a 6-card hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Dompe uses different deck and hand size; would need deck and handRank overrides.

scoring.description: Best poker hand wins the pot. Knocker wins: others pay 2 chips each. Knocker loses: pays 2 chips to each staying player. Folders pay 1 chip to knocker.
scoring.winCondition: Have the highest-ranking five-card poker hand at showdown

synthesis.shortDescription: Knock Poker is a draw-and-discard game where players build the best poker hand and knock to challenge opponents.
